Efficient, effective and economical energy storage is holding back green energy. Wind and solar are intermittent sources that can't be managed during peak demand hours or stored during off-peak hours. The so called "spinning load" generation systems of coal, gas and nuclear are used in conjunction with wind and solar to meet peak demand hours but must be left running during off-peak hours since boilers take time to reach operating temperature. Until we have an effective and economical means of storing energy to use during peak times, renewables just can't fully be the solution. Pumped hydro storage is a good option, but it is not well suited for many areas as it needs large water reservoirs to work. Small pumped hydro units are possible, but they can't handle things on a large scale and nobody wants a bunch of small pumped hydro stations all over their city. Same with storage batteries. Molten salt batteries are dangerous and expensive but better suited for scale than small distributed battery systems (e.g. Tesla's Power Wall) since spreading out the infrastructure just makes more points of failure and less ability to handle demand changes across a large service area. We just don't have a good method to store power so green energy will continue to suffer its shortcomings for the foreseeable future.
